what: Five vertical bands of the background color split the screen and act as the page-transition curtain — on an opened page the covering bands turn straight transparent from the left, each .1s later, over .7s, clicking a link to another page of the same site covers them again from the left, each .05s later, over .15s, and navigates after 450ms (phone 400ms) — a quiet transition for white-background wedding and restaurant sites.

options.out: Duration (seconds) for one strip to turn transparent on open, default .7
options.out-step: Delay between strips when opening (seconds), default .1 — the first strip waits this long too
options.in: Length (s) one band covers when flipping, default .15
options.in-step: Delay between bands when flipping (s), default .05
options.go: Time from press until moving on (s), default .45
options.go-sp: Seconds until the transition below 768px width, default .4
options.wait: Fires when an event with this name occurs on document (such as when the loader ends) — otherwise load
options.widths: Write each band’s width ratio separated by spaces (if given, the band count is that number) — Brand ‹3 23 23 23 23 23 23 3› (ruled cell widths)
options.widths-sp: Width ratio below 768px width — strips beyond the shown count are hidden (reference “1.5 8.6 8.7 8.6 8.6 1.5”)
options.out-delay: Extra seconds to wait before the first band when opening, default 0 (brand .3 — from .325s in steps of .025s)
options.logo: If true, [data-fx-part inside the attached element=logo] moved to the exact center of the curtain, wiped away right→left over 1s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1) when opening, and wiped in after .3s over 1.5s when covering (Brand)

use: <body data-fx="strip-fade-page"> — If you flip pages often like an app, data-fx-strip-fade-page="out: .3; out-step: .03; go: .2"
note: The original puts the grid logo loader (tri-grid-unveil) over the band only on the first visit, and from the next page in the same session only lifts the band. The band changes only opacity, with no curve
